hypothesis: The manifest, session and result layouts that the C compiler lays out equal the bytes that the generator packs, and a generic application replays recorded PCM through the capture interface.

conditions.checks: checks/sunstone-app-abi.py; checks/os-audio-replay.py (AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, AArch64 instruction emulation); checks/os-audio-replay-linked.py (actual linked instructions of a generic application built with an empty MIMUS_DIR; grant publication, liveness, clock, waits, progress and finish modeled)

narrative: Static assertions in include/sunstone_app.h and include/sunstone_session.h fix sizeof(struct ss_manifest)=552, ss_region=56, ss_session_header=64, ss_extent=8, ss_input_fact=40, ss_host_frame=64, ss_result=56, ss_failure=48 and the 592-byte board prefix. checks/sunstone-app-abi.py compiles hello-compute and a synthetic manifest for the host and aarch64-none-elf and compares both sections with the generator. The recorded-PCM replay executes 320 frames, 20 ms of paced waits and an independent Adler-32 checksum. The mimus session with NPU, CPU grant and three INPUT regions is 1,392 bytes; the mimus inputs are 14.2 MB hashed in 4 KiB steps. No board run.

hypothesis: Moving input authentication into the application main task and the host channel into a responder task leaves the staged recorded run and the host transcript collection unchanged within run-to-run variation.
prediction: Admission adds one SHA-256 over the 552-byte manifest per boot. Input authentication hashes the same 14.2 MB of mimus inputs in the same 4 KiB steps, in the main task instead of the recognizer, so the staged recorded run from entry to the first recognition agrees with the earlier time within run-to-run variation. Each ss_* call is a direct function call with atomic accesses and no exception entry. A mimus host request now passes through the responder task, which the USB0 owner wakes with a task notification; a 16 KiB transcript takes 16 reads and a few status queries, so a wake-up of a few microseconds per request adds well under 1 ms to the host's transcript collection time (measured in os-staged-recorded and on the board, before and after).
conclusion: Not yet run: no before-and-after measurement of the staged recorded run or of the transcript collection exists. The migration commits have landed; the comparison remains open work in the design.
narrative: Planned comparison: staged recorded run (os-staged-recorded) from entry to first recognition before and after input authentication moved into the application main task; host transcript collection time before and after the host channel moved behind ss_host_recv and ss_host_send. No figures were recorded.
